co_zone_2.blurb: On the Beyer's Walls in Unaweep Canyon, outside Grand Junction, Zone 2 is the next group of lines along the cliff. It holds 15 single-pitch lines, mostly trad with a few sport routes, and the grades cluster around 5.10 and 5.11 with some 5.9s and one 5.12. The stone is rated highly and the slab climbing here is among the best in the neighbourhood. A small ledge crossing the crag gives a few options for a second pitch from the upper tier. Some of the older protection and anchors have been replaced, but bring a full trad rack and judge each line for yourself.

co_ridge_2.blurb: Ridge 2 is a short crag on Eldorado Mountain, just outside Boulder, with 15 routes of sport and trad mixed together. Grades start with one easy line in the 5.6 range and run mostly through 5.9 to 5.11, with a handful of 5.12s at the top end. The sandstone is clean and edgy, and it sits on a south-facing rib, so it catches plenty of sun. Sport development here dates to the late 1980s and early 1990s. A rope and a small rack of quickdraws covers most of it. It is quieter and less appealing than neighbouring Ridge 4, though a few lines are stout.

co_broken_rock.blurb: Broken Rock sits in Boulder Canyon just across the creek from Castle Rock, and cracks riddle its faces. Of the 14 routes, most are trad crack climbs, with a couple of bolted lines, and they run from 5.9 to 5.12 with the bulk at 5.9 to 5.10. The granite is of similar quality to Castle Rock's, but the walls face north and west on a low tier, so they stay shaded and feel damp, with lichen, moss and bird droppings in places. It sees far fewer climbers than Castle Rock, which suits anyone after a quiet crack day.

_expect.name: Truth or Consequences Crag aka Inca Stone

co_truth_or_consequences_crag_aka_inca_s.blurb: This crag is a short walk off the highway in Boulder Canyon, near the turn to the falls. It mixes bolted lines with traditional ones across 14 mostly single-pitch routes, with the trad climbs needing real gear. Grades range from an easy 5.7 up to 5.11 and one 5.12, with 5.10s and 5.11s making up most of the list. A mossy gully splits the crag into a smaller left side and a bigger right side, and the trail arrives between them. Routes finish at bolted anchors or easy walk-offs. The rock could use more cleaning, so a brush is handy, and watch for poison ivy on the slope.

co_twelve_pack_wall.blurb: Twelve Pack Wall is a section of the main cliff band at North Table Mountain above Golden, the sector just past the prominent Industrial Buttress. It has 14 routes, mostly trad cracks with a few bolted sport lines, spread from easy 5.6 and 5.7 climbing through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, plus a single 5.12. Routes are short, roughly 60 to 80 feet. The wall faces south and sees sun much of the day, which makes it comfortable in cooler weather and hot in summer, with little shade along the base.
